links.outcome: Quality of chatbot renal drug dosing adjustment answers (AQUOS) by renal function and medication complexity
links.effect: AQUOS ranged from -19.0% to 95.2% depending on chatbot; declined with decreasing renal function (ChatGPT: -0.215; P=.03) and increasing medication complexity (Scite: -0.239; P=.02).
links.quote: We found that AQUOS declined with decreasing renal function (ChatGPT: -0.215; P=.03) and increasing medication complexity (Scite: -0.239; P=.02).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot answers across two independent times
links.effect: AI chatbot answers were highly reproducible across two time points; prompting language (English vs German) changed scores by up to 4.8%.
links.quote: The AI chatbot answers were highly reproducible.

links.outcome: Adequacy of chatbot quality for deployment in high-risk renal dosing
links.effect: Even the highest AQUOS achieved is insufficient for deploying AI chatbots in the high-risk health care sector; possible harm rose with lower kidney function and higher medication complexity.
links.quote: Even the highest AQUOS achieved is insufficient for deploying AI chatbots in the high-risk health care sector.

unlisted_practices: Development and validation of a composite quality score (AQUOS) for chatbot drug dosing answers
Assessing potential harm using the WHO patient safety classification framework

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on simulated/retrospective geriatric patient medication queries regarding renal drug adjustments without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
